decisions.rationale: Exhaustive review of all 222 comparators found no feature with the same newtools convenience-state non-authority boundary. The cited routing and single-owner contracts are adjacent authority safeguards, but they govern different state and failure boundaries.

No comparator combines the same MCP/provider owner-subordination, mirrored status vocabulary, and compatibility-alias boundary. Secret custody, MCP degradation, and tool execution ownership are plausible neighboring controls with different authorities and lifecycles.

The anchor uniquely spans headless browser/research evidence retention, redaction, quota, truncation, crash consistency, manifest finalization, and partial-run status. The listed audit, retention-class, teardown, and Firecrawl lifecycles are narrower or differently owned neighbors, not equivalent.

No comparator has the same combined executable provenance, worktree path, Doctor-to-execution TOCTOU, spawn-cwd generation, child-environment, and secret boundary. The listed path, executable, subprocess, and internal-code controls are distinct members or adjacent trust surfaces.

No comparator governs the same preview/build session identity, cancellation, stale-result, and artifact-authorization lifecycle. Projection gating and Approve And Build currentness are adjacent controls with different commands, state boundaries, and failure outcomes.

The anchor's atomic source/auth snapshot and stale-state rejection for Docker and GitHub build/Actions effects is not duplicated. Generic mutation races, publication approval, command registration, and Docker/Kubernetes transactions overlap but differ in product authority or target family.

PF-0080 is merge-equivalent: both govern the debug attachment/grant lifecycle for a bound target, authorization lifetime, target disappearance or replacement, in-flight transitions, and cleanup or recovery races. PF-0079 is the projection of that authority and PF-0215 is command-routing differentiation, so both remain distinct.

The anchor is a cross-cutting authorization-to-dispatch and cleanup-recovery atomicity protocol. Each listed comparator covers only a mutation gate, cleanup/storage atom, distributed dedupe, or autonomy check; those are members or dependencies, not the same lifecycle boundary.

No comparator governs retirement of this deprecated authentication alias with the same detection, telemetry, deadline, version, and acceptance boundary. Retired bridges and reference-only baselines are analogous migration controls for different concepts.

No comparator defines the same Docker auth result payload typing, validation-host normalization, capability ordering, timestamps, versioning, redaction, retention, and consumer authority. Account isolation, auth setup, and route secret custody are related but separate authority and lifecycle contracts.

The exact Docker CLI execution, Hub API management, and Unraid XML storage ownership split is not repeated. Container discovery, infrastructure command families, and generic tool/execution separation are neighboring or umbrella boundaries, not equivalent.

No comparator owns the mandatory repository-creation confirmation dialog and its revalidation, repository-created-elsewhere, permission-loss, and post-confirmation states. General approval synchronization and permission-editor recovery are related UI lifecycles only.

The Build-to-Unraid compound publish workflow has a distinct staged source, commit, push, template, cleanup, resume, and final-state lifecycle. Publication approval and Docker/Kubernetes mutation recovery are plausible neighbors but govern different targets and failure semantics.

No comparator matches the evidence overlay's cross-document precedence, schema-version compatibility, propagation, conflict-resolution, and conformance boundary. Attribution envelopes, capability/audit semantics, and citation contracts are adjacent seams with different state and consumer boundaries.

The anchor jointly requires child lineage preservation and a tool, write, FileSafe, mode, provider/model/account, and crew ceiling before dispatch plus post-run audit. Approval propagation, skill inheritance, delegated-task identity, and tool ownership each cover narrower or differently scoped concerns.

No comparator has the same delegated child/parent web-evidence disclosure boundary spanning URL, headers, cookies, forms, console, sensitive pages, iframes, and retention. Scrub gates, visible-test redaction, context sharing, and capture lifecycle are related but distinct.

The OSI child host-capability clamp and its missing executable fixture form a distinct parent/run-mode/execution-unit/worktree/FileSafe/host-ceiling boundary. General host trust, approval freshness, skill inheritance, and DAE jail isolation do not share the same full lifecycle and oracle.

No comparator contains the same coordination registration/update/unregister contradiction between warn-and-continue prose and fail-fast sample code. Invocation results, dispatch failures, and competing permission algorithms are analogous consistency problems with different authority and failure states.

The SCM projection's repo_root/worktree_path disclosure to GUI and receipt consumers has a distinct local-machine privacy boundary. Sensitive receipts, invocation context, terminal provenance, and disabled reasons expose other data with different producers and lifecycles.

No comparator captures the direct authority conflict between optional ad hoc CLI evidence logs and the canonical unified event stream. Registry observability, terminal durability/privacy, and tool-output retention are separate stores or consumers.

The anchor specifically governs delegated planning-child classification and the parent mode ceiling. General run-mode distinctions, grep availability, and visible permission-gated research overlap but are umbrella or member contracts and do not share the same child lifecycle boundary.

No comparator reproduces the live-GUI versus retired tier ontology contradiction and missing tier-to-graph/package/seam/lane mapping. GUI classification defects, requested/effective disclosure, and remote-planning ambiguity are related but distinct.

The anchor spans raw provider, tool, and LLM payload display and retention with secret detection, redaction truth, access, size, and export. The listed scrub, display, managed-output, and tool-settlement contracts are narrower members or different processing stages.

No comparator permits the same vision_provider configuration field to remain runtime-dead while later requiring no dead fields. Requested/effective disclosure, provider route projections, and future ZDR state are analogous configuration-truth concerns with different fields and outcomes.

No comparator has the same VerificationStatus required-field failure allowed through a general WarnAndContinue policy. Invocation result unions, conditional host-command fields, and dispatch error ordering are nearby validation concerns with different failure semantics.

No comparator reproduces the verification-specific mandate for both canonical seglog/redb persistence and a separately forbidden verification.log. Terminal durability, discovery receipts, and tool-output settlement are adjacent persistence models, not the same conflict.

The crew-board message store and untrusted cross-agent prompt-injection channel have a distinct coordination authority, lifecycle, and consumer boundary. Instruction/mention injection, invocation-context privacy, and delegated-task history are plausible neighbors only.

No comparator combines safe-hook handling, lazy compatibility state, hook budget, and permission fallback as one lifecycle. Target/host trust coverage and final permission rechecks are dependencies or members rather than the same safe-hook envelope.

The PageRepresentation recording contract specifically binds prompt-injection detection, warning chips, visible cards, redaction profile provenance, and sensitive representation references. General scrub, testing display, browser envelope, and capture/share contracts have different state and failure boundaries.

No comparator governs these exact coordination-mirror and GUI-concept historical source-lineage classifications. Retired/reference-only material, canonical state owners, and routing ownership are analogous authority boundaries for different artifacts.

No comparator owns graph-level node-ID uniqueness and dependency referential integrity. Graph approval request identity and GoalRun interfaces are graph/runtime neighbors but address different identities, transitions, and failures.

The anchor is the Plan-node change-budget and overlay policy-mode authority model. Filesystem settings, access precedence, matcher normalization, and tool permission hierarchy are related controls but apply to different records, owners, and enforcement lifecycles.

This is a broad runtime-artifact producer, actor, provenance, authority, and consumer boundary across many artifact classes. The listed attribution, receipt, index, citation, and generated-media contracts are narrower members with distinct producers and failure semantics, so umbrella/member merging is rejected.

This anchor is the cross-artifact retention, privacy, operational-state, and destructive lifecycle umbrella. Sensitive receipts, retention classes, notification receipts, managed outputs, and Firecrawl audits are distinct members with narrower authorities and state transitions.

The anchor specifically owns the versioned HITL approval artifact envelope and semantic decision lifecycle. Permission matching, cascades, replies, scheduler wakeup, and approval persistence are downstream or adjacent approval lifecycles, not the same artifact boundary.

The anchor is the immutable pre-dispatch permission snapshot lineage boundary. Snapshot source completeness, indeterminate recovery snapshots, blocked-invocation optionality, and registry-churn binding are related fields or lifecycle consumers; none has the same complete authority and state boundary.

The anchor is specifically crash-recoverable residue cleanup on logout and project deletion. Account removal, sensitive receipt cleanup, generic retention deletion, and research teardown each overlap only part of that trigger, data set, or recovery lifecycle; umbrella/member merging is rejected.

This positive contract is an umbrella separating ephemeral, scrubbed, exported, and credential-store evidence while enforcing masking, provenance, and no-persist/no-echo. Each listed comparator is a narrower custody, scrub, leakage, display, or receipt member with a different lifecycle.

The storage-owned mutation lock, armed selection version, cancel/complete reconciliation, and auditable explicit override boundary is not duplicated. Generic gate TOCTOU, stale-state modeling, distributed dedupe, and approval freshness are adjacent safeguards with different authorities or missing override lifecycle.

The anchor combines deferred export, compact-header, Doctor, cost-column, and alert-history surfaces with permission, retention, dedupe, stale-link, and partial-write gaps. Export and notification/audit comparators are narrower members rather than the same compound surface lifecycle.

No comparator governs widget layout persistence, concurrent edits, invalid dimensions, removed widget versions, responsive overflow, keyboard manipulation, localization expansion, and account-repair links. Compact accessibility, mutation conflicts, and renderer text behavior are only adjacent concerns.

The anchor owns usage evidence-routing identity conflicts, route-target loss, schema skew, and authorization/redaction differences between exact-record and view exports. Attribution, scrub, history/image export, minimization, and export-manifest contracts are related but have different objects and lifecycles.

No comparator covers the same usage cross-surface GUI matrix and its keyboard, screen-reader, focus, locale, translated-text, reduced-motion, contrast, and offline drill-through fixtures. The listed accessibility contracts govern different surfaces or lower-level renderer behavior.

The usage cache-reporting contract uniquely combines hit-rate denominators, pricing snapshot authority, policy freshness, unavailable copy, cross-account aggregation permission, and revoked/corrected metadata. Web action caches, managed output refs, and provider/cost catalogs have different cache or consumer boundaries.

No comparator owns the user-visible usage anomaly rationale and budget-source attribution with its tenant, authorization, provenance, retention, deletion, redaction, and untrusted-provider boundary. Generic audit, receipt, invocation, and cost data lifecycles are related but distinct.

The optional OTLP/Helicone-style exporter has a distinct endpoint trust, transport, tenant, schema migration, retry, throughput, resource-bound, and non-blocking lifecycle. Export minimization and redacted receipt/tool-output contracts are inputs or neighbors, not equivalent exporters.

The prompt-injected WebCapabilityAffordance owns the bounded modes, seven operations, permission state, lazy registry summary, native-browser primacy, and fallback status. Approval keys, browser action schemas, dispatcher parity, and reader boundaries are consumers or adjacent layers, not the same affordance.

No comparator governs the exact prompt-affordance prohibition on raw secrets, full provider configuration, and provider-private prompt files. Provider-route custody, process leakage, secretless projections, and Firecrawl key lifecycle are neighboring secret controls for different state boundaries.

The nine-persona web-policy envelope jointly binds self-initiation triggers, shared tools, agent reason, permission, visibility, read-only posture, mutation denial, dispatch, and evidence routing. General web approvals, modes, browser authority, research, and dispatcher parity are dependencies or umbrella/member neighbors.

The anchor specifically requires visible web ask/deny decision-card truth and exposes a boolean-only GUI oracle missing content, reason binding, accessibility, focus, and localization. General approval mapping, compact surfaces, denied notices, and batch-host review are related UI contracts with different scopes and state machines.
